origin: Exactly what it says: loading on and on, without end. It's credited to Aza Raskin, who devised it in 2006.
whenToUse: Content that's browsed continuously, such as social feeds or photos.
Lists where discovery matters more than order.
Page buttons are a hassle on mobile.
whenNotToUse: People need to find specific items again (use pagination).
There's a footer below the list people must see (use a load more button).
Search results where sorting and comparing matter.

alternatives.name: Load More
alternatives.reason: Loading only when people ask for it.

alternatives.name: Pagination
alternatives.reason: When people need to remember a position.

accessibility: Announce loading and the last item with role="status".
Keep a Load more button that does the same, for keyboard users and for when automatic detection fails.
The scroll area is a named region, so it can be scrolled with the keyboard.
If the first batch doesn't fill the area, load the next one right away.
